name: Procedural democracy
summary: Procedural democracy defines democracy by its method rather than its results: regular, free and competitive elections with broad suffrage, backed by the freedoms of expression and association that make real contestation possible. It lets citizens remove rulers peacefully and takes no position on economic or social outcomes, which are left to whatever voters and parties settle on. Its best-known thinkers are sceptical that ordinary citizens can govern directly and see their role as choosing and dismissing leaders.
scope: The minimalist or procedural conception of democracy as developed by Joseph Schumpeter (competitive struggle for the people's vote), Karl Popper (democracy as peaceful dismissal of rulers), and Robert Dahl (polyarchy), with Przeworski-style minimalism in the background. Excluded are substantive, participatory and deliberative conceptions, and the pejorative sense of a hollow democracy where procedures are manipulated. Because it is a method, most economic and cultural statements are marked indifferent rather than inferred as positions, so this profile will have many neutral answers.

keyFigures.name: Joseph Schumpeter
keyFigures.role: Economist who defined the democratic method as a competitive struggle for the people's vote

keyFigures.name: Karl Popper
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who defined democracy as government that can be removed without bloodshed

keyFigures.name: Robert Dahl
keyFigures.role: Political scientist who set out the institutions of polyarchy

sources.title: Procedural democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition by procedures such as regular elections on universal suffrage, contrast with substantive democracy, and the critical sense of hollow democracy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The procedural view defines democracy by how decisions are made, so healthcare provision is left to what elected majorities choose.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A method-only conception takes no side on wage policy; it is whatever competing parties and voters settle on.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Dahl treats socioeconomic arrangements as outside the polyarchy criteria, so the ideology itself is indifferent between market and state allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: Procedural democracy is compatible with public or private ownership; the choice is for voters to make through elections.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax rates are a policy outcome that the democratic method leaves to electoral competition, not something the definition prescribes.

unions-good.rationale: Dahl's polyarchy requires an enforceable right to form autonomous associations, which covers unions, though the ideology does not rule on their social value.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights fall under external limits on democracy in SEP, which procedural proponents neither require nor reject.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is an outcome question that the procedural definition leaves open to elected governments.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare levels are decided through the democratic process, and the procedural conception endorses no particular level.

worker-ownership.rationale: An economic-structure question outside a purely political definition of democracy; adherents range across the spectrum.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Polyarchy depends on free expression, association and information not controlled by the government, which mass surveillance can chill; inferred, not directly discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: A social-policy question with no bearing on the procedures that define the ideology.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Dahl's required freedom of expression, including criticism of officials, makes adherents wary of speech restrictions, though the ideology does not address hate speech specifically.

strong-leader.rationale: Popper's test is whether rulers can be removed peacefully; a leader bypassing gridlock and institutional checks undermines the dismissal mechanism.

state-harmful.rationale: Procedural democrats want a state whose institutions let the ruled dismiss rulers, so they treat the state as necessary rather than harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: A policy question left to elected majorities; the procedural conception has no stance.

empower-police-military.rationale: Resourcing coercive forces is an outcome for voters to decide; the ideology only requires they stay under civilian electoral control.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A moral-policy question outside a procedural definition of democracy.

decide-locally.rationale: SEP notes arguments about both local and national scales; the procedural method works at any level so adherents are not committed.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is a policy outcome the ideology leaves to the democratic process.

traditional-family.rationale: Social-moral questions are for voters to resolve; the method itself is neutral.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The procedural conception takes no side on marriage law, treating it as an outcome of electoral choice.

abortion-legal.rationale: A contested moral issue that the ideology leaves entirely to the democratic process.

more-religion-public.rationale: Whether religion plays a larger public role is an outcome for voters, not part of the procedural definition.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: SEP distinguishes procedural from substantive equality goals; a purely procedural view neither demands nor forbids such programmes beyond equal political rights.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A theoretical claim about gender with no connection to democratic procedure.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural preservation is not addressed by a method-based definition of democracy.

gradual-change.rationale: Popper favoured institutions allowing peaceful change of government and piecemeal reform, and inferred adherents lean toward respecting established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: An outcome question left to electoral choice; the procedural view says nothing on migration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Procedural democrats dispute how democratic international bodies are, but the ideology holds no settled view.

free-trade.rationale: An economic policy outcome that the procedural conception does not prescribe.

nation-first.rationale: Foreign-policy orientation is not addressed by the democratic method.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents are divided and the procedural definition covers only domestic decision-making.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed by a procedural definition; the borders of the demos are a separate question.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental-economic policy is left to democratic choice.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: A policy outcome that voters and governments decide; the ideology is indifferent.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: A general claim about technology that is not part of any procedural theory of democracy.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is a matter for elected decision-makers, not the procedural definition.

revolution-justified.rationale: Popper contrasts democracy, where rulers go by election without bloodshed, with tyranny where only revolution removes them, so in a working democracy revolution is unnecessary and unjustified.

experts-over-public.rationale: Schumpeter doubted voters' competence yet still placed the decisive choice in competitive elections, not in expert rule; elected leaders decide, though experts may advise.

central-planning.rationale: Dahl and Schumpeter treated economic systems as separable from the democratic method, so adherents hold no common view.

socialized-markets.rationale: Schumpeter argued socialism and democracy could in principle be combined, so the ideology is indifferent about this economic form.

land-value-tax.rationale: A fiscal design question outside the democratic method.

tax-inheritance.rationale: A tax outcome left to voters under the procedural conception.

basic-income.rationale: A welfare design question that the ideology does not address.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is an outcome of electoral competition, not a procedural matter.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is for elected governments to decide; the procedural conception is neutral.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distribution of property is a substantive matter the procedural view leaves open.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Schumpeter treated democratic competition as workable within a complex modern economy; abolition of wages is not a position of the ideology and sits oddly with it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside the scope of the procedural definition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Schumpeter's model channels power through party competition for the popular vote, not state-recognised producer bodies; inferred as opposed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Popper defines tyranny as rule the ruled cannot dismiss without revolution, and Schumpeter's democratic method requires free competition for the vote, which a ruling single party excludes.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Popper's test of peaceful dismissal is compatible with constitutional monarchy but not with absolute rule, so adherents split by type of monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Procedural democrats value democracy as a method that lets people remove bad rulers without bloodshed, a justification that holds even when voters choose badly, though Schumpeter was more sceptical about voter quality.

direct-votes.rationale: Schumpeter argued the voters' role is to elect leaders and not to instruct them, and judged direct popular rule infeasible in complex societies.

workers-councils.rationale: Schumpeter's democratic method is competition among leaders for votes in general elections; councils replacing parliaments are incompatible with it.

right-to-secede.rationale: The boundary of the demos is a question the procedural method does not settle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Procedural democrats hold that rulers acquire power by winning votes in competition, not by innate fitness, though Schumpeter accepted leadership is exercised by an elite.

political-violence-never.rationale: Popper presents democracy as the arrangement that makes violence unnecessary for changing governments, though no source states an absolute ban.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the procedural conception values war, and its emphasis on peaceful transfer of power points the other way.

separate-church-state.rationale: Procedural definitions do not specify the relation of religion and state; adherents differ.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: SEP notes law-making authority in democracy rests on procedure, but a procedural view is formally neutral on whether elected majorities adopt scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Polyarchy requires constitutionally elected officials to control government policy, which sits uneasily with privatised coercion; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence posture is not addressed by the democratic method.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Dahl's inclusiveness criterion requires practically all adults to have the vote, which does not entail a view on national composition.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Schumpeter wrote on class but his democratic theory centres on competition among leaders, not class conflict as history's driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: SEP contrasts procedural equality with substantive aims; a procedural conception secures equal political participation but not equal outcomes, and adherents differ.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: A substantive claim outside the procedural definition.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed by the democratic method.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Schumpeter's model treats politicians as competing for votes and voters as having vague impulses, describing behaviour rather than endorsing self-interest as moral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Polyarchy rests on enforceable individual rights to speech and association, so a duties-first stance is not an adherent view; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: An ethical claim unrelated to democratic procedure.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed by the democratic method.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

human-enhancement.rationale: Left to voters and legislators; no procedural stance.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Schumpeter and Popper both locate authority in elected, dismissible leaders, so handing decisions to algorithms conflicts with accountability; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Dahl's right to information outside government monopoly bears on this only loosely, so no firm stance is inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Popper favoured piecemeal, testable reform which fits the idea, but procedural democracy as such is a method and takes no stance.

direct-action.rationale: Popper and Schumpeter locate legitimate political change in elections and institutions that allow peaceful dismissal of rulers, not in direct action replacing them.

means-match-ends.rationale: A general ethical maxim that the procedural definition does not address.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed; no connection to democratic procedure.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: SEP discusses a democratic division of labour as a response to the participation problem, so abolition is not an adherent view; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A distributive ideal the procedural view leaves outside its scope.

production-for-use.rationale: An economic-system question outside the procedural definition.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxian economic claim with no place in a procedural theory of democracy.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Popper's criterion defines any government the ruled cannot dismiss without revolution as a dictatorship, which a class dictatorship over former rulers would be.

collective-farming.rationale: Farm organisation is an economic outcome the ideology does not address.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A causal claim outside the procedural conception.

taxation-theft.rationale: Elected governments levy taxes through the method; procedural democracy supplies no view on taxation's morality.

harm-principle.rationale: Required civil rights are tied to contestation, not to a general theory of when the state may restrict adults.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Dahl's rights belong to individuals and associations alike, with no ruling on group rights.

conscription.rationale: A defence-policy question left to elected governments.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Popper and Schumpeter locate the key check on rulers in the vote and peaceful dismissal, so putting exit above voting reverses the core idea.

state-as-business.rationale: Schumpeter likened party competition to a market for votes, but citizens as customers who can leave is not his or Popper's view; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: SEP notes the minimal procedural definition carries no substantive welfare commitment; adherents divide on material preconditions of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: The procedural view holds that electoral competition is where political power is decided; the claim is inferred as one adherents would reject.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inclusiveness for practically all adults implies political equality irrespective of group, though the ideology does not discuss heritability.

organic-representation.rationale: Schumpeter's method has candidates compete for votes of individual citizens through parties, not representation via families and corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: A state directing every area of life would leave no institutions for peaceful dismissal of rulers, which Popper makes the test of democracy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Foreign-policy aims are outside the democratic method.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on personal oaths is not removable by those ruled, the opposite of Popper's democratic criterion.

bound-labor.rationale: Polyarchy's rights of association and inclusive suffrage are inconsistent with legally bound labour; inferred from required liberties.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: An epistemological thesis not addressed by procedural democracy.

universal-morality.rationale: SEP notes proceduralists try to ground democracy without contested moral truths, so the ideology avoids taking a stand.

single-common-good.rationale: Schumpeter explicitly rejects the classical doctrine of a common good and will of the people and defines democracy as competition among leaders instead.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy is left to elected governments.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Schumpeter's method concerns selection of political leaders by competitive vote; extending votes into firms is not part of it, though some theorists do extend democracy; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: A policy question the procedural view leaves to voters.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is an outcome of the democratic process.

economic-freedom.rationale: Dahl found polyarchy has socioeconomic conditions but does not list economic freedom as a criterion, so no common view.

rule-by-example.rationale: Popper's institutional test relies on dismissal mechanisms and laws, not on rulers' moral example; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: The procedural method presupposes a defined demos without settling its boundaries.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign-policy question outside the democratic method.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Eligibility for welfare is an outcome left to voters.

work-for-welfare.rationale: A welfare-design outcome left to the democratic process.

class-collaboration.rationale: Labour relations are outside the procedural definition.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: no source ties democratic procedure to destroying inherited institutions, and its respect for existing institutions points the other way.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Polyarchy requires practically all adults to have the vote and most to be eligible for office, which excludes law that assigns public roles by sex.

ban-interest.rationale: Financial regulation is outside the procedural definition.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inclusive suffrage and eligibility for practically all adults, with rights enforceable, are incompatible with legal racial segregation as a political order.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Schumpeter's account has leaders competing for votes with the people choosing among them, not the state serving one class; Marxist instrumentalism is not shared.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is for elected governments, not the procedural definition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim that has no support in procedural theory, which locates change in elections; inferred rejection.

proportional-representation.rationale: SEP records that proceduralists and others debate district versus proportional systems; the ideology is satisfied by any fair competitive electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A sociological claim outside the democratic method.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Schumpeter described leaders as competing for votes, which can imply self-interest, but the ideology offers no verdict that elites are corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Required rights of association and inclusion make state coercion over reproduction hard to reconcile with polyarchy; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Popper's emphasis on institutions that restrain those in power points to accountability, though legal accountability for past abuses is not discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Polyarchy is neutral on the scope of government as long as elected officials control it.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equal rights for practically all adults conflicts with state discouragement of mixed marriage; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: SEP presents political equality among citizens as the minimal core of democracy, giving equal votes and rights though not a full moral doctrine.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A socialist-theory claim outside the procedural definition.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A legal policy left to democratic decision.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Dahl's rights of expression and association imply freedom to change belief; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A policy outcome left to elected legislatures.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education policy is left to the democratic process.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A strengthening state that never withers conflicts with Popper's stress on institutions limiting rulers; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Popper's democracy rests on the ruled being able to dismiss rulers, a practical form of consent, though Schumpeter doubted any real popular will.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade doctrine is outside the procedural definition.

population-transfer.rationale: Required rights and inclusive citizenship for practically all adults are incompatible with expelling a minority.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian absolute that the procedural view does not adopt.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Schumpeter modelled political life as competition for votes, but the claim here is a broad social theory the ideology does not make.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Popper warned institutions must not be easily destroyed by those in power, while Schumpeter favoured open competition; adherents divide on banning anti-system parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory of liberty not part of the procedural definition.

separated-powers.rationale: Popper requires institutions and traditions that stop rulers from destroying the means of dismissal, which divided power supports, and Dahl notes constitutionally vested control.

vanguard-party.rationale: A permanent vanguard holding power outside electoral dismissal is the kind of government Popper classes as tyranny.

priority-to-poor.rationale: SEP treats distributive priorities as substantive aims, beyond a procedural conception.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A housing policy outcome left to voters.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Dahl's right of association covers unions, but the ideology does not rule on strike law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: A causal claim outside democratic procedure.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Schumpeter's democratic method defines leaders as chosen by competitive election, so lottery replaces the defining mechanism; SEP notes sortition as a rival proposal.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Polyarchy depends on enforceable rights of expression and association; suspending protections against internal enemies erodes the conditions for fair contestation.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic policy is an outcome left to voters.

party-controls-media.rationale: Polyarchy requires access to information not monopolised by the government or any single group, which state or party control of media would deny.

party-commands-army.rationale: Polyarchy vests control of government in elected officials, not a party apparatus commanding the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules are decided by voters and not by the procedural definition.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of representatives is an institutional detail on which the ideology takes no side.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Schumpeter assumed parties as vehicles of competition, but internal discipline is not addressed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Adherents divide on whether supranational unions are democratic enough; no common view.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential versus parliamentary design is open as long as elections control government.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the democratic method.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical authority that cannot be dismissed by election is the non-dismissible rule that Popper classes as tyranny.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Dahl's enforceable freedom of expression conflicts with moral censorship of art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Popper's test is peaceful dismissal; unlimited re-election is acceptable if elections stay free, but concern about entrenchment divides adherents.

recall-officials.rationale: Schumpeter rejected voters instructing representatives between elections, while Popper's dismissal logic favours easy removal; adherents are split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Foreign policy is outside the democratic method.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing law is a policy outcome left to voters.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Territorial unification is not addressed by a method-based definition of democracy.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Schumpeter doubted ordinary voters' political rationality, but the claim about the educated is not part of the theory.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

death-penalty.rationale: Criminal-justice policy is decided through the democratic process.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum content is a policy outcome.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum content is a policy outcome the ideology does not address.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Expression rights bear on this, but adherents divide on pornography specifically.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not defined by the procedural conception.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is an outcome left to elected governments.

religious-exemptions.rationale: A policy question on which the procedural view is silent.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's view is a liberal one, while procedural democracy requires expression rights but takes no stand on social conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: An international economic policy outside the procedural definition.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

constituent-assembly.rationale: A democratically elected assembly fits the procedural ideal of legitimate authority through elections, though the ideology does not discuss constitution-writing.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Polyarchy's defining criteria include free and fair elections with expression and association rights, so suspending political freedoms contradicts it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global distributive duties are substantive questions outside the procedural definition.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Polyarchy requires elected officials control policy but allows presidential or parliamentary designs, so adherents have no common view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Insulating a bank from elected governments is a design choice on which democratic theorists divide.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial diplomacy is not addressed by the procedural definition.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Schumpeter denied a single common good in politics, and property doctrine is outside the method.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A historical-theoretical dispute outside the procedural conception.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is a policy outcome left to elected decision-makers.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is not part of the procedural definition.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception, although consent of the people is a related concern.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not defined by democratic procedure.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Polyarchy allows both ceremonial and executive heads of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The procedural method presupposes a defined demos and does not settle whether force may preserve its borders.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements are left open as long as elected officials control government.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A ruler regarded as sacred is not one the ruled can dismiss, contrary to Popper's criterion for democracy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is a policy outcome the ideology leaves to voters.

character-from-environment.rationale: A psychological theory outside democratic procedure.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Popper holds that social institutions and traditions must ensure rulers cannot destroy the means of their dismissal, which a ruler unbound by law could do; Dahl likewise requires constitutional control.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

mixed-constitution.rationale: SEP discusses mixed and balanced arrangements, but the procedural definition does not require them.

leader-cult.rationale: A cult of the leader as embodiment of the nation sits badly with Popper's view of rulers as dismissible office-holders; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law policy is a matter for voters and not the procedural definition.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine unrelated to the procedural conception.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is a substantive outcome the ideology neither requires nor forbids.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: nothing in a procedural conception supports such claims and it concerns internal decision-making only.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Polyarchy requires enforceable freedom of expression and association, which punishing departure from a faith would violate.

women-must-cover.rationale: State compulsion over dress conflicts with the freedoms Dahl lists as institutions of polyarchy; inferred, as dress codes are not discussed.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed by the procedural definition.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority arrangements are left open by a procedural view.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A theory of history outside democratic procedure.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is an outcome left to voters.

no-bailouts.rationale: Fiscal and financial policy are left to elected governments.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: SEP distinguishes internal limits that protect the democratic process from external ones; procedural democrats accept courts protecting the process even against a majority, but not all constraints.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas are a substantive equality measure on which procedural democrats divide.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is an economic policy beyond the procedural definition.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-treaty content is outside the procedural conception.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: A small armed group seizing the moment is the revolutionary route that Popper says democratic institutions make unnecessary.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal inclusion of practically all adults in voting and office-holding conflicts with hereditary political privilege, though economic aspects are not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curriculum content is a policy outcome.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Polyarchy requires inclusiveness and government by elected officials, which tutelage by outside rulers denies; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education policy is left to elected governments.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: A substantive equality question on which procedural democrats are divided.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is outside the procedural definition.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Schumpeter argued capitalism would be undermined by its own success, so the ideology's founder is not a clear adherent; inferred at low confidence.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed by the procedural conception.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist claim outside democratic procedure.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Procedural democracy requires equal political rights but takes no position on private discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: SEP describes internal limits protecting speech and association as consistent with democracy, and Dahl lists these rights as required institutions, which a bill of rights secures.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: A question of international law outside the procedural conception.

elective-rulers.rationale: Popper's definition of democracy is that rulers can be dismissed by general election, and Schumpeter defines it as competition for the people's vote, so rulers chosen by election is the core claim.

minority-veto.rationale: SEP notes unanimity rules favour the status quo, and procedural democracy rests on decisions binding dissenters through vote counts.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Popper's democratic institutions exist to dismiss rulers peacefully; lawful resistance is secondary and adherents prefer electoral removal.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The ideology requires elected control of government but not parliamentary supremacy over other designs.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: An ethical claim outside the democratic method.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A policy question left to elected decision-makers.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A conservative social ethic not addressed by the procedural conception.

notes: Many statements are marked 0 with low confidence because the procedural conception is deliberately silent on policy outcomes; expect weak salience. Strands differ: Schumpeter was sceptical of voters, Dahl stressed rights and pluralism, and Popper emphasised peaceful change.
